gaps.sentence: The two sides struggled to ___ an agreement before the deadline.
He ___ a serious accident on his motorbike last year.
gaps.explanation: have an accident is the fixed collocation for being involved in one.

gaps.sentence: Most children learn to ___ the time before they start school.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: ___ the time (read a clock)
gaps.explanation: tell the time means to be able to read a clock; it is a fixed expression.

gaps.sentence: We ___ our shopping at the local market every Saturday.
gaps.explanation: do the shopping is the collocation for buying food and household goods.

gaps.sentence: The thief ran so fast that no one could ___ him.
gaps.hint: to capture someone who is running away
gaps.explanation: catch somebody means to capture or seize them after chasing.

gaps.sentence: Let me ___ a photo of you both.
gaps.explanation: take a photo/picture is the fixed collocation for photographing something.

gaps.sentence: Ordering your food online can ___ you a lot of time.
gaps.explanation: save somebody time means to make it possible for them to use less time.

gaps.sentence: The scientists are ___ research into new forms of energy.
gaps.explanation: do research (into something) is the collocation; 'make research' is wrong.
